Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Random-string "tokens" as barcoded stimulation history
ideas.description: The material is a series of short random tokens of varying length and character composition. Treat it as an analogy for barcoding: give cells a brief, distinct AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., anisomycin, TPA, or EGF) and record each cell's history with a heritable lineage barcode or fluorescent reporter. After a washout of days to weeks, test whether the original stimulus can be read out from chromatin accessibility (scATAC) and from the transcriptional response to a second challenge.

ideas.title: Priming and re-stimulation memory assay with ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq
ideas.description: Stimulate cells once, wash out, rest them for several cell cycles, then re-stimulate. Compare the transcriptional kinetics and magnitude of the second response with those of naive cells (RNA-seq, nascent RNA). Map the retained AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and accessibility at enhancers with ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN, and test whether the sites that stay open predict which genes respond faster.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation at defined times (dTAG/AID)
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged FOS or JUN to remove AP-1 at set times after the initial stimulus. Removal after the stimulus ends but before re-challenge tests whether AP-1 itself must persist to maintain memory, or whether it is only needed to establish it. Measure whether accessibility and the enhanced second response persist without AP-1.

ideas.title: Single-cell live imaging of AP-1 dynamics and heritability
ideas.description: Image FOS/JUN reporters or endogenously tagged proteins in lineages over several divisions, using microfluidic pulse protocols that vary pulse number, duration and spacing. Quantify whether the dynamics of a mother cell predict those of its daughters, and whether the second-response amplitude depends on the pattern of earlier pulses, which would suggest a history-dependent state rather than a transient one.

ideas.title: Pioneer-like activity and chromatin-mark causality tests
ideas.description: Check whether AP-1 recruits chromatin remodelers (BAF) and deposits H3K27ac or H3K4me1 at memory enhancers, and whether those marks persist after AP-1 is gone. Use dCas9-based epigenome editing to add or remove the marks at specific enhancers, or use an AP-1 motif mutation, and measure the effect on memory of the response. This separates AP-1 as the mark-writing trigger from the chromatin state as the carrier of memory.
